dateMeaning: Repository research-series label, not an upstream release date or a claim that a moving documentation page was current on that date. GitHub source observations are commit-pinned below.

requestedWorkflow.matching: Rank/filter a small wordlist and optionally preview bounded one-step typo variants; cryptographic verification is exact.

discovery.privacy: Only generic public engine names were searched. No owner private key, candidate, hint or fingerprint was sent to metasearch.

services.role: SearXNG instance directory, not a cryptographic engine
services.observed: Directory accessible; search.utilibre.org listed. Instance presence/rating does not certify privacy, engine compatibility or cryptographic safety.
Homepage accessible. JSON query fetch failed; HTML general query returned no results. Not a comprehensive search or a negative engine-support finding.

services.role: Tool catalog; actual metasearch is search.utilibre.org
services.observed: IT query mostly irrelevant; general query mixed results including Sequoia. Used only to discover authoritative sources, not as a feature/support matrix. Catalog privacy descriptions were not independently audited.

engines.name: OpenPGP.js
engines.runtime: Existing pinned browser engine, unmodified module; Node/browser distributions are the same engine
engines.finding: The workbench wraps existing secret-packet decrypt and validation APIs. Default high-level decryptKey validation need not validate every subkey; the recovery wrapper validates every included secret packet sequentially and returns only a matching candidate index.
engines.appProfile: v4 RSA-2048-16384, v4 legacy Ed25519/Curve25519 or v6 Ed25519/X25519; AES + iterated salted SHA-1/SHA-2 S2K, SHA-1 integrity or standard AEAD. Argon2/stubs/unprotected/mixed/unsupported inputs refused.
engines.execution: Synthetic Node and shipped-browser-module tests plus actual Chromium worker controls; not owner-key or physical-device certification.

engines.name: GnuPG
engines.runtime: Native engine; GPGME is a high-level integration library, not a separate OpenPGP implementation
engines.finding: Key-management and controlled passphrase interfaces exist. Use a separately reviewed native integration, never shell-interpolate candidates or use an owner's default home/agent. gpgv is signature verification only and cannot establish private-key recovery.
engines.execution: Existing classic-v4 native harness extended to check exact candidates against a fresh GnuPG-protected re-export. Full gpg/gpgconf unavailable locally; mandatory exact-head CI must run it without skips. No GnuPG v6, GUI, owner-key or mobile recovery claim.

engines.name: Sequoia OpenPGP / sq / sqop
engines.runtime: Rust library with separate CLI/SOP tools, not a browser drop-in
engines.finding: Projects page describes an RFC 9580 implementation, sq key/certificate operations and sqop SOP. sqv is a detached-signature verifier. The fetched status page explicitly dates itself 2024-10-02 and is not treated as a current-version feature matrix.
engines.execution: Source/documentation review only; no Sequoia binary, build, license integration or recovery test executed in this change.

engines.name: RNP / librnp
engines.runtime: C++ engine with a C API and selectable native crypto backends
engines.finding: rnp_key_unlock accepts an exact password/provider, with separate key-protection queries. RFC-9580-related algorithms depend on build flags/backend; crypto-refresh and PQC options are documented off by default at this pin. A generic RNP name is not proof a packaged binary supports the desired v6/S2K/AEAD profile.
engines.execution: Commit-pinned source review only; not compiled or linked into the app.

engines.name: rPGP
engines.runtime: Pure-Rust OpenPGP library with low-level APIs
engines.finding: README and implementation checklist claim RFC 9580/v4/v6, PKESKv6/SKESKv6/SEIPDv2 support. A source checklist is not an independently executed interoperability result or a guarantee for every consumer application.
engines.execution: Commit-pinned source review only; no Rust/WASM binary or recovery backend added.

engines.name: Bouncy Castle Java bcpg
engines.runtime: Java OpenPGP library, separate from provider/FIPS products
engines.finding: Pinned README identifies bcpg RFC 4880/RFC 9580 support; PGPSecretKey.extractPrivateKey uses a supplied decryptor and returns null for missing private material. The general specification webpage still lists older RFCs, so do not infer a full v6 support matrix from that page or a FIPS certificate.
engines.execution: Commit-pinned source review only; no Java/Android implementation or GUI/device recovery test added.

engines.name: ProtonMail/go-crypto; GOpenPGP wrapper
engines.finding: The repository already has a separate pinned, test-only independent native v6 interoperability harness. GOpenPGP wraps go-crypto and is not a second independent implementation. That message harness does not certify owner protected-key passphrase recovery.
engines.execution: Existing four mandatory native-v6 tests, separate from this new recovery UI; no Go engine shipped in the browser.

decision: Keep the pinned, unmodified OpenPGP.js browser engine and bounded local recovery worker. Do not add runtime switching, native binaries, remote dictionaries, metasearch requests or secret uploads. Future engines require version/build-flag/license review and independent protected-key negative/positive tests before integration.
unchangedGates: PUBLIC keyring and full fingerprint/binding/revocation recipient policy
original keys and existing encrypted backups
encrypted APK delivery and unrelated deployment gates
